chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from his father, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed three or two. He said: “He builds upon the lesser number, acts upon certainty, and after finishing he recites a light tashahhud; likewise in the beginning of the salat (prayer) and its end.”

The correct way of understanding this report is that he only builds upon the lesser number when his supposition inclines toward it, and he completes his salat (prayer) as a precaution. But when the supposition is balanced, then building upon the greater number is more precautious, if he completes after finishing the salat (prayer) as we have explained. What confirms what we have said is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Abā al-Ḥasan, peace be upon him
key_terms.النُّقْصَانِ: the lesser number in the count of rakʿahs
key_terms.الْأَكْثَرِ: the greater number in the count of rakʿahs
key_terms.الْجَزْمِ: certainty or what is firmly established
key_terms.الْوَهْمِ: supposition or uncertainty regarding the prayer count
key_terms.تَشَهُّدًا: the testimony recited in the sitting of salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if he doubts whether he prayed two rakʿahs or three?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling for doubt in the number of rakʿahs during salat (prayer), especially between two and three. It presents the principle of acting on certainty and discusses a juristic reconciliation that distinguishes between a dominant supposition and equal doubt.
